newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums slump on growing supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums slump on growing supply.

text.p: NWE gas oil declined with IPE futures on Wednesday, but premiums slipped too on the prospect of increased supply from the Mediterranean and the United States and reluctance from buyers holding out for lower prices.
Nov IPE closed down $3 at $227.50 per tonne as bulls took fright at the approach of a fleet of cargoes of heating oil from the United States, heralding easier supply fundamentals.
"And apart from the increased availability there was a feeling that the market was simply overdone," one trader said.
Heating oil barge premiums fell by $3 per tonne, trading at $235.50-237.75 fob Rotterdam, equivalent to Nov IPE +$3.50.
Heat cargoes were offered at Tuesday's traded level of IPE Nov $7 cif, but found no response.
Buyers were waiting for the arrival of cargoes from the Mediterranean to bring prices lower.

The prospect of diesel cargoes from the south also put pressure on these premiums, which slumped around $6 to Nov IPE +$30/33, although no trade was concluded. One trader said bids were as much as $15 under offers.
